question: A breast lesion classified as BI-RADS 4 on mammography or ultrasound carries an intermediate suspicion for malignancy (2–95%) and requires tissue sampling (biopsy) for definitive diagnosis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. BI-RADS 4 (suspicious) mandates tissue sampling. Compare: BI-RADS 3 (probably benign, <2% malignancy risk) is followed with short-interval imaging; BI-RADS 5 (highly suspicious) goes directly to biopsy with surgical planning.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. BI-RADS 4 lesions are suspicious and require biopsy. The category is subdivided into 4A (low suspicion, 2–10%), 4B (moderate suspicion, 10–50%), and 4C (high suspicion, 50–95%) to guide biopsy urgency and clinical correlation.
